## 1. Run the instruments

```sh
fathom research report --since 168h [--service <svc>] [--json]
fathom instrument --adoption [--json]
fathom plans status --service <svc>
```

`fathom research report` (docs/design/research-flywheel.md) is the
flywheel's single-command aggregate: everything `instrument --adoption`
covers (call log + `.fathom/observations.md`) PLUS injection coverage and
obligations-served counts from the hooks beat log, and context-bench
token/turn deltas when a bench artifact exists — one report, written to
`workspace/artifacts/research/report.{md,json}` as well as printed. Prefer
it over ad-hoc log tailing or re-running `instrument --adoption` alone; fall
back to `instrument --adoption` directly only if you need its exact legacy
field names or don't need the beat-log/bench sections. Neither replaces
`plans status` (still the only source for plan-freshness) or a direct read
of `.fathom/observations.md` (still the only way to list *which* frictions
are open — both report only counts).

`instrument --adoption` is a deterministic-given-inputs report over the MCP
call log (`workspace/logs/mcp-calls.jsonl` by default) plus
`.fathom/observations.md` — a snapshot of one window, never a trend, unless
you explicitly diff two runs. `plans status` is always **derived from the
index**, never asserted — the same "done means proven" discipline the
`fathom-verify` skill runs at push time, viewed as a rollup.

## 2. The honesty rules — apply these to every sentence you write

These are not suggestions; they are the discipline that keeps this skill
from becoming a fathom advertisement instead of a measurement:

1. **Report only what the instrument measured.** If `instrument --adoption`
   didn't count it, don't claim it. "Fathom made this session faster" is not
   a sentence this skill is allowed to write unless a benchmark
   (`context-bench`, `docs/design/coding-agent-excellence.md` §0.5) actually
   measured it for the comparison being made — and even that headline
   number has already been revised down once (the original "≤1/10th the
   discovery tokens" claim was retracted to a measured 1.38–1.79× after
   re-running the bench for real; the win is real but smaller than the
   first draft claimed). Quote measured numbers, not vibes.
2. **State the predates-instrumentation split, every time it's nonzero.**
   `verify_gate_catch_count` (JSON) / the "gate catches" line (table)
   counts only verify/review calls that carry a `verdict_outcome`.
   `verify_gate_predates_instrumentation` counts calls from a binary built
   before that field existed — their outcome is genuinely unrecoverable
   from the log. **Never fold the second number into the first.** Say
   "N catches measured this window (plus M earlier calls whose outcome
   predates instrumentation and can't be recovered)," not just "N catches."
3. **Never attribute an outcome the data can't support.** A high
   `claims_attach_hit_rate` means `brief` calls came back with claims
   attached more often — it does NOT mean those claims changed anyone's
   decision, and it is not evidence of time saved. Don't infer causation
   ("this caught a bug that would have shipped") the log cannot show.
4. **`call_log_read: false` means "never observed," not "measured zero."**
   An absent or unreadable call log is a distinct state from real,
   confirmed zero traffic — say so explicitly rather than reporting a flat
   0 that reads as a measurement.
5. **Zero-call tools are a fact, not automatically a verdict.** A
   registered tool with zero calls this window may be genuinely unused, or
   may just not have come up yet — list it, don't editorialize past what
   the count shows.
6. **Always end with the open frictions.** `instrument --adoption` reports
   only the open-observation *count*
   (`open_observation_count`/`observations_path`, JSON). To name them, read
   `.fathom/observations.md` directly and list the `### O<N> — <title>`
   entries whose `- **Status:**` line still starts with "open" — oldest
   first. **Every impact narration ends with this list as the flywheel's
   ask.** A report that only celebrates wins without naming what's still
   broken is an incomplete report, not an honest one — if `fathom observe`
   hasn't been run recently, say that too (see the `fathom-feedback`
   skill).

## 3. What to include

A complete narration touches, in this order:

1. **Window covered** — the call-log path and whether it was readable at
   all (rule 4).
2. **Injection traffic** — per-surface `surface_traffic` totals, and the
   `brief` claims-attach hit rate (with `nil`/undefined stated plainly when
   there were zero `brief` calls in the window — never a fabricated 0%).
3. **Gate catches** — `verify_gate_catch_count` with the predates-split (rule 2).
4. **Plan freshness** — `fathom plans status`'s proven / claimed-unproven /
   open / deferred / other-skipped rollup, per plan.
5. **Zero-call tools** — the list, stated as a fact (rule 5).
6. **Open frictions** — the flywheel's ask (rule 6). Non-negotiable, even
   when everything else in the report is good news.


## The observatory and the brief

For the at-a-glance version of everything above, open the daemon's
observatory: `http://127.0.0.1:7575/observatory` (fleet wiring/freshness/
traffic with remedy commands), `/observatory/impact` (catches and
discovery with denominators; the counterfactual pilot state machine).
`fathom brief --print` renders the same model as a shareable markdown
value brief with an explicit "Not measured" section — write it, read it,
and let a HUMAN decide where it goes (law 13).
